title.zh: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 39: Gan Wenkun, Fan Chengmo, Ma Xiongzhen, Fu Honglie
title.raw: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈

sentences.zh: 列傳三十九

translations.literal: Biographies 39
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 39

sentences.zh: =甘文焜=甘文焜，字炳如，漢軍正藍旗人，其先自豐城徙瀋陽。

translations.literal: Gan Wenkun, styled Bingru, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner; his ancestors had moved from Fengcheng to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenkun, whose style was Bingru, belonged to the Han military company of the Plain Blue Banner. His forebears had relocated from Fengcheng to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 父應魁，從入關，官至石匣副將。

translations.literal: His father Yingkui followed the army through the pass into China and rose to deputy commander at Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingkui entered China with the conquering armies and eventually became deputy commander at Shixia.

sentences.zh: 文焜善騎射，喜讀書，尤慕古忠孝事。

translations.literal: Wenkun was skilled at riding and archery, loved reading, and especially admired ancient tales of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun excelled at horsemanship and archery, loved books, and was especially drawn to stories of loyalty and filial devotion from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 以官學生授兵部筆帖式，累遷禮部啟心郎，屢奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed a clerk in the Board of War, was promoted repeatedly to Qixinlang in the Board of Rites, and on many missions won imperial praise.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an academy student, he became a clerk in the Board of War and rose through the ranks to Qixinlang in the Board of Rites, earning repeated commendation on diplomatic assignments.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授大理寺少卿，遷順天府府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he was made vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review and then transferred to be prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he was appointed vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review and later became prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 崇文門榷稅不平，疏劾之。

translations.literal: The transit duties at Chongwen Gate were unjust; he memorialized impeaching the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the transit duties at Chongwen Gate unjust, he submitted a memorial impeaching those responsible.

sentences.zh: 廷議令兼攝，文焜曰：「言之而居之，是利之也。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that he should hold the post concurrently; Wenkun said, "To speak against it and then occupy it is to profit from it."
translations.idiomatic: When the court proposed that he take charge of the post himself, Wenkun said, "To denounce the abuse and then hold the office would be to profit from it."

sentences.zh: 」固辭。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，授直隸巡撫，奏复巡歷舊制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed governor of Zhili and memorialized to restore the old system of touring inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became governor of Zhili and memorialized to revive the former practice of provincial inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 單車按部，適保定、真定所屬諸縣患水災，疏請蠲歲賦。

translations.literal: Traveling alone in a light carriage on his rounds, it happened that the counties under Baoding and Zhending suffered flood; he memorialized requesting remission of the year's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Touring his jurisdiction in a simple carriage, he found counties under Baoding and Zhending stricken by flood and memorialized for remission of the annual land tax.

sentences.zh: 總督白秉真以賑費浩繁，請聽官民輸銀米。

translations.literal: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, citing the vast cost of relief, requested permission for officials and people to contribute silver and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, citing the enormous cost of relief, asked that officials and commoners be allowed to contribute silver and grain.

sentences.zh: 文焜斥廉俸以助。

translations.literal: Wenkun spent his entire official salary to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun donated his entire official salary to the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 議敘，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On review of merit he was given the additional rank of vice-president of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his service he was granted the additional title of vice-president of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷雲貴總督，駐貴陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, with headquarters at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and took up residence at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂鎮雲南，欲藉邊釁固兵權，詭報土番康東入寇，紿文焜移師，又陰嗾凱里諸苗乘其後。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui held Yunnan and wished to use border incidents to consolidate military power; he falsely reported that the tribal people of Kangdong had invaded, deceived Wenkun into shifting troops, and secretly incited the Miao of Kaili to strike from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui then held Yunnan and sought border troubles to tighten his grip on the army. He fabricated a report that the Kangdong tribes had raided, lured Wenkun into moving his forces, and secretly stirred the Kaili Miao to attack from behind.

sentences.zh: 文焜策康東無能為，凱里近肘腋，不制將滋蔓，先督兵搗其巢，斬苗酋阿戎。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged that Kangdong could do little harm but that Kaili lay close at hand and, if unchecked, would spread; he first led troops to destroy their lair and beheaded the Miao chief Arong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun reckoned Kangdong posed little threat, but Kaili lay at his very flank and would spread if left alone. He marched first against their stronghold and beheaded the Miao chief Arong.

sentences.zh: 既平，約雲南會剿康東。

translations.literal: Once pacified, he arranged with Yunnan for a joint campaign against Kangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he arranged a joint campaign with Yunnan against Kangdong.

sentences.zh: 三桂慮詐洩，謂康東已遠遁，繇是益憚之。

translations.literal: Sangui feared his deception would leak out and claimed Kangdong had already fled far away; from this he feared Wenkun all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui, fearing exposure of his ruse, claimed Kangdong had already fled into the distance—and from that point feared Wenkun all the more.

sentences.zh: 文焜巡歷雲、貴各府州皆遍。

translations.literal: Wenkun toured every prefecture and department in Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun made inspection tours through every prefecture and department in Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，遭母憂，上命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he suffered his mother's death; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died; the emperor permitted him to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 文焜又遣兵擊殺臻剖苗酋阿福。

translations.literal: Wenkun again sent troops to attack and kill Afu, chief of the Zhenpo Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun again sent troops against the Zhenpo Miao and killed their chief Afu.

sentences.zh: 疏乞歸葬，許給假治喪。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging leave to return home for burial; leave to conduct the funeral was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking leave to return home for the burial, and was granted a leave of absence for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 三桂請以雲南巡撫兼督篆，令督標兵悉詣雲南受節度，而以利啗之，冀為己用。

translations.literal: Sangui requested that he also hold the seal as governor of Yunnan, ordered all troops under the governor-general's banner to go to Yunnan for his command, and tried to win him with profit, hoping to make him his own man.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui asked that Wenkun also hold the Yunnan governorship, ordered all troops of the governor-general's command to Yunnan under his direction, and tried to buy him off, hoping to turn him to his cause.

sentences.zh: 十二年，文焜還本官，適撤籓議起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wenkun resumed his original post, just as discussion of abolishing the feudatories arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wenkun returned to his post just as the court began debating the abolition of the feudatory princedoms.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，殺巡撫硃國治，遣其黨偪貴陽。

translations.literal: Sangui rebelled, killed Governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his partisans to press Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui rose in rebellion, killed the Yunnan governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his followers to threaten Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 文焜聞變，使族弟文炯齎奏入告，牒貴州提督李本深率兵扼盤江。

translations.literal: On hearing the uprising Wenkun sent his clansman Wenkong to carry a memorial to the capital, and dispatched orders to Guizhou Provincial Commander Li Benshen to lead troops and hold Pan River.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the revolt, Wenkun sent his cousin Wenkong with a memorial to the capital and ordered Guizhou commander Li Benshen to hold the Pan River line with his troops.

sentences.zh: 本深已懷貳，先以書覘文焜意。

translations.literal: Benshen already harbored disloyal thoughts and first sent a letter to probe Wenkun's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Benshen was already disloyal and first wrote to sound out Wenkun's intentions.

sentences.zh: 文焜手書報之，期效張巡、南霽雲誓死守，而本深不之顧。

translations.literal: Wenkun replied in his own hand, pledging to emulate Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun in vowing to die defending the city, but Benshen paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun answered in his own hand, vowing to follow Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun in holding the city to the death—but Benshen ignored him.

sentences.zh: 本標兵已受三桂餌，紛潰弗聽調。

translations.literal: Ben's banner troops had already taken Sangui's bribes and scattered in disorder, refusing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Benshen's troops had already accepted Sangui's bribes and broke ranks, refusing to obey.

sentences.zh: 文焜度貴陽不可守，令妾盛率婦女七人自經死，獨攜第四子國城赴鎮遠，思召湖北兵扼險隘，使賊不北出。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged Guiyang indefensible, ordered his concubine Sheng to lead seven women to hang themselves, and alone took his fourth son Guocheng to Zhenyuan, planning to summon Hubei troops to hold the passes and keep the rebels from marching north.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Guiyang could not be held, Wenkun had his concubine Sheng lead seven women of the household to hang themselves, then set out alone with his fourth son Guocheng for Zhenyuan, hoping to rally Hubei troops at the mountain passes and block the rebels' advance north.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申朔，癸卯至鎮遠，守將江義已受偽命，拒弗納。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, day bingshen, on day guimao he reached Zhenyuan; the defending commander Jiang Yi had already accepted rebel appointment and refused him entry.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month (day bingshen) he reached Zhenyuan on day guimao, but the garrison commander Jiang Yi had already accepted a rebel commission and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 文焜渡河至吉祥寺，義遣兵圍之。

translations.literal: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple; Yi sent troops to surround him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple, where Yi sent troops to surround him.

sentences.zh: 文焜望闕再拜，拔佩刀將自殺，國城大呼請先死，奪其刀以刎而還之，屍乃踣，血濺文焜衣。

translations.literal: Wenkun bowed twice toward the palace, drew his sword to kill himself; Guocheng cried out asking to die first, seized the blade and cut his own throat, then returned it; his body fell, blood splashing Wenkun's robe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun bowed twice toward the capital, drew his sword to take his own life. Guocheng cried that he should die first, seized the blade, cut his own throat, and handed the sword back; as his body fell, blood spattered Wenkun's robes.

sentences.zh: 文焜曰：「是兒勇過我！

translations.literal: Wenkun said, "This boy was braver than I!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun said, "That boy was braver than I!"

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺，年四十有二。

translations.literal: " He then killed himself, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took his own life. He was forty-two.

sentences.zh: 從者筆帖式和善雅圖殉。

translations.literal: His attendant clerk Heshanyatu died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His clerk Heshanyatu died with him.

sentences.zh: 亂平，貴州巡撫楊雍建以文焜治績及死事狀上聞，予優恤。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, Guizhou Governor Yang Yongjian reported Wenkun's administrative achievements and manner of death; generous posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, Guizhou governor Yang Yongjian reported Wenkun's record in office and his death in service, and the court granted generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 遣其長子宣化同知國均迎喪還京師，使內大臣佟國維迎奠盧溝橋，贈兵部尚書，諡忠果。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guojun, sub-prefect of Xuanhua, was sent to bring the coffin back to the capital; Inner Minister Tong Guowei was ordered to receive it at Lugou Bridge; he was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous name Zhongguo.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guojun, sub-prefect of Xuanhua, was sent to bring the coffin to Beijing; Inner Minister Tong Guowei received it at Lugou Bridge. Wenkun was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous name Zhongguo (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 建祠貴陽，上賜「勁節」二字顏其額。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Guiyang; the emperor bestowed the two characters "Steadfast Integrity" to inscribe its tablet.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was erected at Guiyang, and the emperor inscribed its tablet with the words "Steadfast Integrity."

sentences.zh: 子七，國璧尤知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Guobi was especially well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Guobi was especially renowned.

sentences.zh: 國璧，字東屏，以任子授陝州知州，改蘇州同知，擢山西平陽、浙江寧波知府，名循吏。

translations.literal: Guobi, styled Dongping, as son of an official was made prefect of Shaanzhou, transferred to sub-prefect of Suzhou, promoted to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang, famed as an upright local administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Guobi, styled Dongping, entered office by hereditary privilege as prefect of Shaanzhou, became sub-prefect of Suzhou, and rose to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang, earning a reputation as a model official.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，幸杭州，御書硃子詩及「永貞」額以賜。

translations.literal: On the Sacred Ancestor's southern tour, when he visited Hangzhou, he personally wrote a Zhu Xi poem and the plaque "Ever Faithful" as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi Emperor's southern tour, when he visited Hangzhou, he personally wrote out a poem of Zhu Xi and bestowed the plaque "Ever Faithful."

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「汝父盡節，朕未嘗忘，此為汝母書也。

translations.literal: He instructed him: "Your father died in loyalty; I have never forgotten. This inscription is for your mother."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Your father died loyal to the throne, and I have never forgotten. This inscription is for your mother."

sentences.zh: 」累遷雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: " He was promoted repeatedly to governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose through successive promotions to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，起為正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was recalled as commander of the Han Banner of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was recalled to serve as commander of the Han company of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，授綏遠城右翼副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was made deputy lieutenant-general of the Right Wing at Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Qianlong reign he was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the Right Wing at Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 复罷。

translations.literal: He was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: =范承謨=范承謨，字覲公，漢軍鑲黃旗人，文程次子。

translations.literal: Fan Chengmo, styled Jingong, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, second son of Fan Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengmo, whose style was Jingong, belonged to the Han military company of the Bordered Yellow Banner and was the second son of Fan Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，選庶吉士，授弘文院編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was selected as a bachelor and appointed compiler in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler in the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was made governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時去開國未久，民流亡未復業，浙東寧波、金華等六府荒田尤多。

translations.literal: The founding was not long past; the people had fled and not returned to their fields; in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures of Ningbo, Jinhua, and others had especially much wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was still young, refugees had not yet returned to their farms, and in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures including Ningbo and Jinhua held especially large tracts of abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 總督趙廷臣請除賦額，上命承謨履勘。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen requested reduction of tax quotas; the emperor ordered Chengmo to conduct an on-site survey.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen petitioned to reduce tax quotas, and the emperor ordered Chengmo to survey the land in person.

sentences.zh: 承謨遍歷諸府，請免荒田及水沖田地賦凡三十一萬五千五百馀畝。

translations.literal: Chengmo toured every prefecture and requested exemption of tax on wasteland and flood-damaged fields totaling more than 315,500 mou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo toured every prefecture and petitioned to exempt more than 315,500 mou of wasteland and flood-damaged fields from taxation.

sentences.zh: 杭州、嘉興、湖州、紹興四府被水，民飢，承謨出布政使庫銀八萬，糴米湖廣平糶，最貧者得附老弱例，肩鹽給朝夕，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: The four prefectures of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing suffered flood; the people starved; Chengmo took 80,000 taels from the provincial treasury, bought grain in Huguang and sold it at fair price; the poorest were allowed under the aged-and-infirm rule to carry salt for daily sustenance; very many were saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When flood struck Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing, Chengmo drew 80,000 taels from the provincial treasury, bought grain in Huguang, and sold it at fair prices. The poorest were allowed, under the relief rule for the aged and infirm, to carry salt for their daily bread, and a great many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 並疏請「漕米改折，石銀一兩。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting: "Convert grain tribute to silver payment at one tael per shi.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Convert grain tribute payments to silver at one tael per shi.

sentences.zh: 明年麥熟，補徵白糧，以三年帶徵。

translations.literal: When wheat ripens next year, collect the white-grain quota in arrears, to be levied over three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the wheat harvest comes next year, collect the white-grain quota in arrears over three years.

sentences.zh: 災重者如例蠲免」。

translations.literal: Where disaster is severe, remit according to precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Where the disaster is severe, grant remission as usual."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: Imperial approval was granted and the measures carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and the measures were implemented.

sentences.zh: 十年，以疾請解職，召還。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he requested leave from office on grounds of illness and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to resign on account of illness and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 總督劉兆麒、提督塞白理疏言浙民請留承謨一百五十馀牒，給事中姜希轍、柯聳，御史何元英等亦言：「承謨受事三載，愛民如子，不通請謁饋遺。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and Provincial Commander Saibaili memorialized that the people of Zhejiang had submitted more than 150 petitions asking Chengmo to remain; Censors Jiang Xizhe, Ke Song, He Yuanying, and others also said: "Chengmo has held office three years, loves the people as his children, and will not accept visits, petitions, or gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and commander Saibaili reported that the people of Zhejiang had submitted more than 150 petitions begging Chengmo to stay. Censors Jiang Xizhe, Ke Song, He Yuanying, and others wrote: "Chengmo has served three years, loving the people as his own children, and refuses all lobbying and gifts.

sentences.zh: 劾罷貪墨，廉治巨猾，剔除加耗、陋規、私派諸弊。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed the corrupt, punished major villains with integrity, and eliminated surcharges, irregular fees, and unauthorized levies.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached corrupt officials, punished powerful wrongdoers, and rooted out surcharges, irregular fees, and unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: 浙民愛戴，深於飢渴。

translations.literal: The people of Zhejiang love and honor him more deeply than hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhejiang cherish him as they would food and water in famine.

sentences.zh: 」上命承謨留任。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Chengmo to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Chengmo to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，承謨复疏言湖、嘉兩府白糧加耗，多寡不一，請每石加四斗五升為限；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chengmo again memorialized that surcharges on white grain in Huzhou and Jiaxing varied in amount and requested a limit of four dou five sheng per shi;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chengmo memorialized again that surcharges on white grain in Huzhou and Jiaxing varied widely, and asked that they be capped at four dou and five sheng per shi;

sentences.zh: 又奏蠲溫、台二衛康熙九年以前逋賦及石門、平陽未完輕齎月糧：皆下戶部議行。

translations.literal: he also memorialized remission of arrears before the ninth year of Kangxi for the two garrisons of Wenzhou and Taizhou and unpaid light-transport monthly grain for Shimen and Pingyang: all were referred to the Board of Revenue for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked remission of tax arrears before Kangxi 9 for the Wenzhou and Taizhou garrisons and unpaid transport grain for Shimen and Pingyang—all referred to the Board of Revenue for approval.

sentences.zh: 十月，擢福建總督，疏辭未允，請入覲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian; his memorial declining was not accepted; he requested an audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian. His refusal was not accepted, and he asked to appear before the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，至京師，入對。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached the capital and had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached Beijing and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 承謨疾未癒，命御醫診視，賜藥餌。

translations.literal: Chengmo's illness had not healed; the emperor ordered imperial physicians to examine him and bestowed medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo had not yet recovered; the emperor sent imperial physicians and bestowed medicines.

sentences.zh: 疾稍差，趣赴官，賜冠服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: When his illness improved slightly he was urged to take up his post and was given court dress and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved slightly, he was urged to take up his post and was given court dress and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 福建總督初駐漳州，至是以將撤籓，命移駐福州。

translations.literal: The Fujian governor-general had first been stationed at Zhangzhou; now, because the feudatories were to be abolished, he was ordered to move headquarters to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian governor-general had originally been based at Zhangzhou; now, with the feudatories about to be abolished, he was ordered to move his headquarters to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，承謨察精忠有異志，時方議裁兵，承謨疏請緩行。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengmo perceived that Jingzhong harbored disloyal intent; troops were then under discussion for reduction; Chengmo memorialized asking delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengmo saw that Geng Jingzhong harbored rebellious intent. As the court debated troop reductions, Chengmo memorialized asking that the cuts be postponed.

sentences.zh: 又報巡歷邊海，欲置身外郡，便徵調防禦。

translations.literal: He also reported touring the coastal border, wishing to place himself in an outer prefecture to facilitate mobilization for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported plans to tour the coast and station himself in an outlying prefecture where he could more easily mobilize for defense.

sentences.zh: 事未行而精忠叛，陽言海寇至，約承謨計事。

translations.literal: Before this could be carried out Jingzhong rebelled, falsely claiming sea bandits had arrived, and invited Chengmo to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could act, Jingzhong rebelled, falsely claiming pirates had appeared, and summoned Chengmo to consult with him.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉秉政附精忠，趣同行。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingzheng sided with Jingzhong and urged him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingzheng had joined Jingzhong and pressed Chengmo to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 承謨知有變，左右請擐甲從，承謨曰：「眾寡不敵，備無益也。

translations.literal: Chengmo knew trouble was afoot; his attendants asked him to don armor; Chengmo said, "We are outnumbered; preparation would do no good."
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo knew something was wrong. His attendants urged him to wear armor, but he said, "We are badly outnumbered; armor would do no good."

sentences.zh: 」遂往。

translations.literal: " He then went.
translations.idiomatic: " He went anyway.

sentences.zh: 精忠之徒露刃相脅，承謨挺身前，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's men bared blades to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's men drew their blades to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and cursed them without stopping.

sentences.zh: 精忠拘之土室，加以桎梏，絕粒十日，不得死。

translations.literal: Jingzhong confined him in an earthen cell, put him in fetters, and starved him for ten days, yet he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong locked him in an earthen cell in fetters and starved him for ten days, yet he would not die.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣秉政說降，承謨奮足蹴之僕，叱左右掖之出，曰：「賊就僇當不遠，我先褫其魄！

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent Bingzheng to persuade surrender; Chengmo kicked him down with his foot, shouted for attendants to drag him out, and said, "The rebels' execution is not far off—I will first strip them of their courage!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong sent Bingzheng to urge him to submit. Chengmo kicked him to the ground and ordered his men to drag him out, crying, "The rebels will soon face execution—I will break their spirits first!"

sentences.zh: 」為賊困逾二年，日冠賜冠，衣辭母時衣，遇朔望，奉時憲書一帙懸之，北鄉再拜。

translations.literal: " Held captive by the rebels for more than two years, each day he wore the court cap the emperor had granted, dressed in the clothes he wore when bidding his mother farewell; on new and full moon he hung a volume of the calendar, bowed twice toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: " Imprisoned by the rebels for more than two years, he daily wore the court cap and robes the emperor had bestowed, still dressed in the clothes he had worn when taking leave of his mother. On the first and fifteenth of each month he hung up the official calendar and bowed twice toward the north.

sentences.zh: 所居室迫隘，號曰蒙谷。

translations.literal: The room where he lived was cramped; he called it Menggu (Dark Valley).
translations.idiomatic: His cell was cramped; he called it the Dark Valley.

sentences.zh: 為詩文，以桴炭畫壁上。

translations.literal: He composed poetry and prose, writing on the walls with torch charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry and prose on the walls in charcoal from a pine torch.

sentences.zh: 時有部曲張福建者，手刃奪門入，連斬數賊，力竭死。

translations.literal: At the time a retainer Zhang Fujian, blade in hand, seized the gate and entered, cut down several rebels in succession, and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: One of his retainers, Zhang Fujian, fought his way through the gate with a blade, cut down several rebels in succession, and died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人嘛尼為偽散騎郎，精忠遣守承謨，感承謨忠義，謀令出走。

translations.literal: The Mongol Mani served as a false Gentleman Cavalier; Jingzhong sent him to guard Chengmo; moved by Chengmo's loyalty and righteousness, he plotted to help him escape.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol named Mani held a false commission as Gentleman Cavalier and was assigned to guard Chengmo. Moved by Chengmo's loyalty, he plotted to help him escape.

sentences.zh: 事泄，精忠將磔之，大言曰：「吾寧與忠臣同死，不原與逆賊同生！

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Jingzhong was about to dismember him; he cried out: "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!"
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Jingzhong was about to dismember him. He cried out, "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!"

sentences.zh: 十五年，師克仙霞關，精忠將降，冀飾詞免死，懼承謨暴其罪。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army took Xianxia Pass; Jingzhong was about to surrender and hoped to gloss over his crimes to escape death, fearing Chengmo would expose them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year imperial forces took Xianxia Pass. Jingzhong was about to surrender and hoped to excuse his crimes and save his life, fearing Chengmo would expose them.

sentences.zh: 九月己酉朔，甲子夜半，精忠遣黨偪承謨就​​縊。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, day jiyou, at midnight on day jiazi, Jingzhong sent his partisans to force Chengmo to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month (day jiyou), at midnight on day jiazi, Jingzhong sent his men to force Chengmo to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 幕客嵇永仁、王龍光、沈天成，從弟承譜，下至隸卒，同死者五十三人。

translations.literal: Staff members Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, down to clerks and runners—fifty-three died together.
translations.idiomatic: His secretaries Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, and Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, and servants down to the lowest runners—fifty-three died with him.

sentences.zh: 語互詳忠義傳。

translations.literal: Their stories are given in detail in the Loyalty and Righteousness biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Their stories are told at length in the biographies of loyal martyrs.

sentences.zh: 舊役王道隆奉遣他出，還至延平，聞變，自刎死。

translations.literal: An old servant Wang Daolong had been sent on another mission; returning to Yanping, he heard of the tragedy and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: An old servant, Wang Daolong, had been sent away on business. When he returned to Yanping and heard what had happened, he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 賊焚承謨屍，棄之野，泰宁騎兵許鼎夜負遺骸藏之。

translations.literal: The rebels burned Chengmo's corpse and cast it in the wild; Taining cavalryman Xu Ding carried the remains away by night and hid them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned Chengmo's body and left it in the open country. A Taining cavalryman named Xu Ding carried off the remains by night and hid them.

sentences.zh: 十六年，喪還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the coffin was returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his coffin was brought back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上遣內大臣侍衛迎奠，贈兵部尚書、太子少保，諡忠貞，御書碑文賜其家。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an Inner Minister and guards to receive the coffin; he was posthumously made Minister of War and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with posthumous name Zhongzhen; the emperor personally wrote an epitaph for his family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an Inner Minister and guards to receive the coffin. Chengmo was posthumously made Minister of War and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhongzhen (Loyal and Steadfast), and the emperor wrote an epitaph for his family.

sentences.zh: 十九年，精忠伏誅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Jingzhong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Jingzhong was executed.

sentences.zh: 赴市曹日，承謨子時崇臠其肉祭墓。

translations.literal: On the day he was taken to the execution ground, Chengmo's son Shichong cut flesh from his body to offer at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jingzhong was led to execution, Chengmo's son Shichong cut flesh from his body as an offering at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 福建民請建祠祀之，御書「忠貞炳日」扁於楣。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian requested a shrine to worship him; the emperor wrote the plaque "Loyal and Steadfast, Shining as the Sun" for its lintel.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian petitioned for a shrine in his honor, and the emperor inscribed its lintel with the words "Loyal and Steadfast, Bright as the Sun."

sentences.zh: 承謨所為畫壁集，上親制序。

translations.literal: For Chengmo's collected writings from the painted walls, the emperor personally composed a preface.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote a preface for Chengmo's collected writings from the prison walls.

sentences.zh: 時崇，字自牧。

translations.literal: Shichong, styled Zimu.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, whose style was Zimu.

sentences.zh: 以難廕出知遼陽州，遷直隸順德知府，有惠政。

translations.literal: By privilege for his father's martyrdom he became prefect of Liaoyang, was transferred to be prefect of Shunde in Zhili, and governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege granted for his father's martyrdom he became prefect of Liaoyang, later served as prefect of Shunde in Zhili, and earned a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to provincial judicial commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to provincial judicial commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，上顧謂群臣曰：「此開國名臣孫，殉難忠臣子也！

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience the emperor turned and said to the ministers: "This is the grandson of a founding minister and the son of a loyal martyr!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave of the throne, the emperor turned to the assembled ministers and said, "Here is the grandson of a founding minister and the son of a loyal martyr!"

sentences.zh: 」四十七年，擢廣東巡撫，兼鹽政。

translations.literal: " In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, concurrently overseeing the salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: " In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong and given charge of the salt administration.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢福建浙江總督。

translations.literal: Two years later he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，入為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he entered the capital as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was recalled to serve as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 命出塞築莫代察罕廋爾、鄂爾齋圖杲爾台站凡四十有七所。

translations.literal: He was ordered beyond the frontier to build forty-seven courier stations at Modai Chahan'ao'er and E'erzhai Tu'ao'er.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered beyond the frontier to establish forty-seven courier stations at Modai Chahan'ao'er and E'erzhai Tu'ao'er.

sentences.zh: 又明年，還朝。

translations.literal: The year after that he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 閩人思其德，附祀承謨祠。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian remembered his virtue and added him to worship in Chengmo's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian, remembering his virtue, added him to the shrine honoring Chengmo.

sentences.zh: =馬雄鎮=馬雄鎮，字錫蕃，漢軍鑲紅旗人，鳴佩子。

translations.literal: Ma Xiongzhen, styled Xifan, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner, son of Mingpei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiongzhen, whose style was Xifan, belonged to the Han military company of the Bordered Red Banner and was the son of Mingpei.

sentences.zh: 以廕補工部副理事官，歷遷左僉都御史、國史院學士。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a deputy director in the Board of Works, and was promoted through Left Vice Censor and academician of the State Historiography Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by hereditary privilege as a deputy director in the Board of Works and rose to Left Vice Censor and academician of the State Historiography Academy.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was made governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上，改廣西。

translations.literal: Before taking up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時群盜蝟起，構瑤、僮掠梧州、平樂二府，不數月討平之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere; Yao and Zhuang incited raids on Wuzhou and Pingle prefectures; within a few months he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising on every side, and Yao and Zhuang raiders plundered Wuzhou and Pingle. Within a few months he had suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 累疏請平鹺價，建學宮，定有司邊俸，省軍糧運費，並罷諸採買累民者，皆得旨允行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to stabilize salt prices, build a Confucian school, fix frontier salaries for local officials, reduce military grain transport costs, and abolish various procurement levies burdening the people—all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly to stabilize salt prices, build a Confucian school, fix frontier salaries for local officials, cut military grain transport costs, and abolish burdensome procurement levies—all approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孫延齡以廣西叛應之，圍雄鎮廨，脅降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in response, besieged Xiongzhen's yamen, and tried to force his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in support of Wu Sangui, besieged Xiongzhen's headquarters, and tried to force him to submit.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫無標​​兵，雄鎮督家人拒守。

translations.literal: The governor had no banner troops; Xiongzhen led his household in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The governor had no troops at his command; Xiongzhen led his household in the defense.

sentences.zh: 密令守備易友亮赴柳州趣提督馬雄來援，弗應。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered garrison commander Yi Youliang to go to Liuzhou and urge Provincial Commander Ma Xiong to come to the rescue; Ma did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered garrison commander Yi Youliang to hurry to Liuzhou and summon commander Ma Xiong to the rescue, but Ma Xiong did not respond.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮自經，為家人救免，以蠟丸馳疏請兵。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his family; he sent a wax-sealed memorial urgently requesting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his family. He sent an urgent wax-sealed memorial begging for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 延齡诇知之，幽雄鎮，置家人別室。

translations.literal: Yanling learned of it through spies, imprisoned Xiongzhen, and placed his family in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling learned of this through his spies, imprisoned Xiongzhen, and confined his family in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 三桂使招降，雄鎮不為屈。

translations.literal: Sangui sent men to persuade surrender; Xiongzhen would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui sent envoys to win him over, but Xiongzhen would not submit.

sentences.zh: 會傅弘烈勸延齡反正，延齡躊躇未決，雄鎮得以間遣長子世濟齎疏詣京師，友亮導之出，客楊啟祥護行，至贛州，江西巡撫董衛國以聞。

translations.literal: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to return to loyalty, Yanling hesitated undecided; Xiongzhen seized the interval to send his eldest son Shiji with a memorial to the capital; Youliang guided him out, guest Yang Qixiang escorted the journey; reaching Ganzhou, Jiangxi Governor Dong Weiguo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to defect back to the Qing, Yanling hesitated. Xiongzhen used the opening to send his eldest son Shiji with a memorial to Beijing. Youliang guided him out, Yang Qixiang escorted him, and at Ganzhou Jiangxi governor Dong Weiguo reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 上遣使護入京，至，授世濟四品京卿。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an escort to bring him to the capital; on arrival Shiji was made a fourth-rank metropolitan official.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an escort to bring him to Beijing, and on his arrival Shiji was appointed a fourth-rank metropolitan official.

sentences.zh: 居數月，雄鎮又具疏陳粵西可復狀，付長孫國楨，俾與客硃昉鑿垣出。

translations.literal: After several months Xiongzhen again prepared a memorial on the recoverable situation in western Guangdong, gave it to his eldest grandson Guozhen, and had him and guest Zhu Fang break through the wall to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Xiongzhen prepared another memorial on how western Guangdong could be recovered and gave it to his grandson Guozhen, who with the guest Zhu Fang broke through the wall to escape.

sentences.zh: 既，又遣州人唐守道、唐正發潛負次子世永出，次第詣京師。

translations.literal: Afterward he again sent natives Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa secretly to carry out his second son Shiyong, who in turn reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa to smuggle out his second son Shiyong, who also made his way to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 又為延齡知，係其孥於獄。

translations.literal: Yanling learned of this again and imprisoned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling discovered this, he threw Xiongzhen's family into prison.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮憤自剄，復為賊所奪，幽之別室。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen in anger cut his own throat but was again seized by the rebels and confined in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: In his fury Xiongzhen cut his own throat, but the rebels seized him again and locked him in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，三桂遣其從孫世琮殺延齡，擁雄鎮至賊壘，迫使降，雄鎮大呼曰：「吾義守封疆，不能寸斬汝以報國，死吾分也！

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Sangui sent his grandnephew Shizong to kill Yanling, brought Xiongzhen to the rebel camp, and tried to force his surrender; Xiongzhen cried out: "By duty I guard the frontier; I cannot cut you down inch by inch to repay the state—death is my portion!"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Sangui sent his grandnephew Shizong to kill Yanling and dragged Xiongzhen to the rebel camp to force his surrender. Xiongzhen cried out, "It is my duty to guard this frontier. I cannot cut you down to serve the throne—death is what I owe!"

sentences.zh: 」賊戕其幼子世洪、世泰怵之，罵益厲，賊殺之，時年四十有四。

translations.literal: " The rebels killed his young sons Shihong and Shitai to intimidate him; he cursed all the more fiercely; the rebels killed him; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels killed his young sons Shihong and Shitai to break his spirit, but he only cursed them more fiercely, and they killed him. He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 從者馬雲皋、唐進寶、諸兆元等九人同時死，妻李，妾顧、劉，女二人，世濟妻董、妾苗，並殉。

translations.literal: Nine attendants including Ma Yungiao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died at the same time; his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao—all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Nine attendants including Ma Yungiao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him, as did his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, and Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao.

sentences.zh: 語互詳列女傳。

translations.literal: Their stories are given in detail in the biographies of exemplary women.
translations.idiomatic: Their stories are told at length in the biographies of exemplary women.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮屍暴四十馀日，友亮收其骸骨，藁葬焉。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen's corpse lay exposed more than forty days; Youliang gathered his bones and gave them a straw burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen's body lay exposed for more than forty days before Youliang gathered his bones and gave them a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮被縶三年，日著書賦詩。

translations.literal: Held captive for three years, Xiongzhen wrote books and composed poetry each day.
translations.idiomatic: During three years of captivity, Xiongzhen wrote and composed poetry every day.

sentences.zh: 既死，客孫成、陳文煥乘間脫走，抵蒼梧，以所著擊笏樓遺稿及匯草辨疑歸世濟。

translations.literal: After his death guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan seized an interval to escape, reached Cangwu, and returned to Shiji his posthumous manuscripts Jiba Lou and Huicao Bianyi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan escaped to Cangwu and delivered to Shiji his surviving manuscripts, Jiba Lou and Huicao Bianyi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，弘烈以雄鎮死狀入告，命議卹。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported Xiongzhen's death; orders were given to deliberate posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported how Xiongzhen had died, and the court ordered deliberation on posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 擢世濟大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Shiji was promoted to vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was promoted to vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 成以舉人授同知，文煥授知縣。

translations.literal: Cheng was made sub-prefect as a provincial graduate; Wenhuan was made magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was appointed sub-prefect as a provincial graduate, and Wenhuan was made a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 旋又授友亮、守道、正發、啟祥游擊、守備有差。

translations.literal: Soon Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were also given ranks as colonel and garrison commander in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were soon given ranks as colonel and garrison commander according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，世濟如廣西迎雄鎮喪至京師，贈太子太傅、兵部尚書，諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring Xiongzhen's coffin to the capital; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring his father's coffin to Beijing. Xiongzhen was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 三桂既平，歲正，上宴群臣，特命世濟及陳啟泰子汝器至御座前賜酒。

translations.literal: After Sangui was pacified, at the New Year banquet the emperor specially ordered Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi before the imperial seat to receive wine.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui's rebellion was crushed, at the New Year banquet the emperor summoned Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi before the throne to receive wine in special honor.

sentences.zh: 世濟官至遭運總督，世永曆運使；

translations.literal: Shiji rose to governor of Zhaoyun; Shiyong became transport commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Shiji rose to governor of Zhaoyun, and Shiyong became transport commissioner;

sentences.zh: 國楨官江南常鎮道，督餉入藏，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Guozhen served as intendant of Changzhen circuit in Jiangnan, supervised grain transport into Tibet, and died on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen served as intendant of the Chang-Zhen circuit in Jiangnan, supervised grain shipments into Tibet, and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: =傅弘烈=傅弘烈，字仲謀，江西進賢人。

translations.literal: Fu Honglie, styled Zhongmou, was a native of Jinxian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Honglie, whose style was Zhongmou, came from Jinxian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明末，流寓廣西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he wandered and settled in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming dynasty he took refuge in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 順治時，以總督王國光薦，授韶州同知，遷甘肅慶陽知府。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign, on recommendation of Governor Wang Guoguang, he was made sub-prefect of Shaozhou and transferred to be prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Governor Wang Guoguang, he became sub-prefect of Shaozhou and later prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂蓄逆謀久，康熙七年，弘烈密以告，逮治，坐誣，論斬。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had long harbored rebellious designs; in the seventh year of Kangxi Honglie secretly reported it; he was arrested, convicted of false accusation, and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had long plotted rebellion. In the seventh year of Kangxi, Honglie secretly reported him, was arrested, convicted of false accusation, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 九年，上特命減死戍梧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor specially ordered his sentence reduced to exile at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor commuted his sentence to exile at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及三桂反，將軍孫延齡、提督馬雄以廣西叛應之。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, General Sun Yanling and Commander Ma Xiong rebelled in Guangxi in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rebelled, General Sun Yanling and commander Ma Xiong joined the revolt in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 弘烈欲集兵圖恢復，陽受三桂偽職，入思州、泗城、廣南、富川諸土司，歷交阯界，募義軍得五千人，遂移檄討賊，從尚可喜軍規肇慶。

translations.literal: Honglie wished to gather troops to recover the province; he outwardly accepted a false post from Sangui, entered the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed into Annam, recruited five thousand volunteers, then issued a proclamation against the rebels and joined Shang Kexi's army to threaten Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie sought to raise troops to recover the province. He outwardly accepted a false commission from Sangui, traveled among the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed into Annam, and recruited five thousand volunteers. He then issued a proclamation against the rebels and joined Shang Kexi's army in a move on Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 三桂甚惎之，使馬雄如柳州害其家百口。

translations.literal: Sangui hated him deeply and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to destroy his family of a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui hated him bitterly and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to slaughter his entire family of a hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 弘烈說延齡反正。

translations.literal: Honglie persuaded Yanling to return to loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie urged Yanling to defect back to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕軍贛州，弘烈密致書言延齡妻孔四貞，定南王有德女，未忘國恩，延齡可招撫。

translations.literal: Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Wu Youde, had not forgotten the state's grace and Yanling could be won over.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was stationed at Ganzhou. Honglie wrote secretly that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Wu Youde, still remembered the dynasty's favor and that Yanling could be won back.

sentences.zh: 又致書奉詔招撫督捕理事官麻勒吉，言王師速進南安，弘烈自韶州策應，則兩粵可定。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Imperial Commissioner Malleji for Pacification and Recruitment, saying that if imperial troops advanced quickly on Nan'an and Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, both Guangdong and Guangxi could be secured.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Imperial Commissioner Malleji, urging that if imperial troops advanced quickly on Nan'an while Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, both Guangdong and Guangxi could be recovered.

sentences.zh: 舒恕、麻勒吉先後以聞，上嘉其忠誠，授廣西巡撫、徵蠻滅寇將軍，俾增募義兵，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Shushuo and Malleji reported in succession; the emperor praised his loyalty, made him governor of Guangxi and General for Subduing Barbarians and Destroying Bandits, and authorized him to recruit more volunteers and act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Shushuo and Malleji reported his actions in turn. The emperor praised his loyalty, appointed him governor of Guangxi and General for Subduing Rebels and Destroying Bandits, and authorized him to recruit volunteers and act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 弘烈克梧州，下昭平、賀、鬱林、博白、北流、陸川、興業諸州縣，進复潯州，遣平樂知府劉曉齎疏上方略。

translations.literal: Honglie took Wuzhou, reduced Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, Xingye and other districts, advanced to recover Xunzhou, and sent Pingle Prefect Liu Xiao with a memorial on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie captured Wuzhou and took Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, Xingye, and other districts. He advanced to recover Xunzhou and sent Pingle prefect Liu Xiao to the capital with a strategic memorial.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保，並加曉參議道。

translations.literal: On review of merit he was made Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and Liu Xiao was given the rank of participation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and Liu Xiao was promoted to participation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 當是時，馬雄據柳州，三桂諸將分據平樂、南寧、橫州，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou and Sangui's generals held Pinglo, Nanning, and Hengzhou in division; their power was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou while Sangui's generals occupied Pinglo, Nanning, and Hengzhou; rebel strength was formidable.

sentences.zh: 弘烈雖屢捷，惟新軍缺砲馬，假於尚之信，弗應。

translations.literal: Though Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked cannon and horses; he asked Shang Zhixin for them but received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Although Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked artillery and horses. He asked Shang Zhixin for help but received none.

sentences.zh: 吳世琮既殺延齡，陷平樂，襲弘烈梧州，弘烈擊敗之。

translations.literal: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling and took Pinglo, he attacked Honglie at Wuzhou; Honglie defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling and seized Pinglo, he attacked Honglie at Wuzhou, but Honglie drove him off.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與將軍莽依圖圍平樂，戰失利，弘烈與互訐。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he joined General Mangyitu in besieging Pinglo; the battle went badly and Honglie and Mangyitu accused each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he joined General Mangyitu in besieging Pinglo. The battle went badly, and Honglie and Mangyitu exchanged accusations.

sentences.zh: 詔謂弘烈兵未支俸餉，奮勇收復諸路。

translations.literal: An edict said Honglie's troops received no pay yet fought bravely to recover every route.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Honglie's troops fought bravely to recover lost territory though they received no government pay.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖自平樂退賀縣，又言糧乏，再退梧州，使弘烈所复郡縣盡棄於賊，因飭莽依圖圖效。

translations.literal: Mangyitu retreated from Pinglo to Hexian, again citing lack of grain, retreated again to Wuzhou, and all the districts Honglie had recovered were abandoned to the rebels; the court therefore ordered Mangyitu to achieve results.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu withdrew from Pinglo to Hexian, then citing lack of supplies retreated again to Wuzhou, leaving all the districts Honglie had recovered to the rebels. The court ordered Mangyitu to show results.

sentences.zh: 弘烈督兵進，賊數万渡左江，弘烈戰敗。

translations.literal: Honglie led troops forward; tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River; Honglie was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie advanced with his troops, but tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 賊陷藤縣，逼梧州。

translations.literal: The rebels took Tengxian and pressed Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Tengxian and threatened Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，之信軍至，弘烈分兵水陸，乘賊攻城時三面夾擊，賊潰​​走，遂下藤縣，克平樂，進复桂林。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived; Honglie divided forces by land and water, and while the rebels were besieging the city struck them on three sides; the rebels broke and fled; he then took Tengxian, captured Pinglo, and advanced to recover Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived. Honglie divided his forces by land and water and, while the rebels were besieging the city, struck them on three sides. The rebels broke and fled. He retook Tengxian, captured Pinglo, and advanced to recover Guilin.

sentences.zh: 弘烈密疏言延齡舊部宜善為解散，又言之信怙惡反覆，當早為之所。

translations.literal: Honglie secretly memorialized that Yanling's old troops should be properly disbanded, and that Zhixin, relying on past crimes and given to reversal, should be dealt with early.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie memorialized in secret that Yanling's former troops should be properly disbanded and that Zhixin, habitually treacherous, should be checked before he turned again.

sentences.zh: 馬雄死，子承廕仍附三桂，受偽封懷寧公，詭言乞款附，弘烈許之，為疏聞。

translations.literal: When Ma Xiong died, his son Chengyin still followed Sangui, received the false title Duke of Huaining, falsely claimed he wished to submit, Honglie agreed and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Xiong died, his son Chengyin remained with Sangui, took the false title Duke of Huaining, and pretended to seek surrender. Honglie accepted this and reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔授承廕昭義將軍統其眾。

translations.literal: An edict made Chengyin General of Manifest Righteousness to command his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Chengyin General of Manifest Righteousness to command his troops.

sentences.zh: 弘烈規取雲、貴。

translations.literal: Honglie planned to take Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie planned an advance into Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，次柳州，承廕期弘烈會議，弘烈至，承廕以其眾叛，襲破其營，執送貴陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year he halted at Liuzhou; Chengyin arranged a meeting with Honglie; when Honglie arrived Chengyin rebelled with his troops, stormed and broke his camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year he halted at Liuzhou. Chengyin invited him to a conference, and when Honglie arrived Chengyin turned his troops against him, overran his camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世璠誘以偽職，弘烈曰：「爾祖未反時，吾已劾奏，料汝家必為叛逆。

translations.literal: Shifan tried to entice him with a false post; Honglie said, "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already impeached him and foresaw your house would prove traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan tried to win him with a false commission. Honglie said, "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already impeached him. I knew your family would turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 汝敢以此言污我邪？

translations.literal: How dare you try to stain me with such words?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you try to defile me with such an offer?"

sentences.zh: 」世琮百計說之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: " Shizong tried every means to persuade him; he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong tried every argument to win him over, but Honglie only cursed him more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 十月辛丑，遇害。

translations.literal: On day xinchou in the tenth month he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou in the tenth month he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月，征南將軍穆佔复貴陽，收遺骸，以死狀聞，贈太子太師、兵部尚書，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Southern Expedition General Mu Zhan recovered Guiyang, gathered the remains, reported his death; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Southern Expedition General Mu Zhan recovered Guiyang, gathered Honglie's remains, and reported his death. Honglie was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，允廣西巡撫郝浴請，建雙忠祠於桂林，祀弘烈及馬雄鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, granting Guangxi Governor Hao Yu's request, a Twin Loyalty shrine was built at Guilin to worship Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, at the request of Guangxi governor Hao Yu, a Twin Loyalty shrine was built at Guilin honoring Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：方諸籓盛強，朝廷所置督撫，勢不足以相抗。

translations.literal: Commentary says: When the feudatories were at their height, the governors and governors-general the court appointed were not strong enough to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the feudatory princes were at the height of their power, the governors the court appointed were not strong enough to stand against them.

sentences.zh: 文焜雖與三桂分疆而治，所部貳於三桂久矣。

translations.literal: Though Wenkun governed a separate territory from Sangui, his command had long since turned disloyal to the court and sided with Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wenkun governed a separate territory from Sangui, his own troops had long since gone over to the rebel.

sentences.zh: 若承謨之於精忠，雄鎮之於延齡，皆同城逼處，惟以身殉，無他術也。

translations.literal: As with Chengmo against Jingzhong and Xiongzhen against Yanling, all lived in the same city pressed close upon the rebel; only martyrdom remained—no other course.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Chengmo facing Jingzhong and Xiongzhen facing Yanling lived in the same cities as their enemies and had no recourse but to die for their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 弘烈異軍特起，又與莽依圖相失，勢孤，遂困於承廕。

translations.literal: Honglie rose as a separate force, fell out with Mangyitu, stood alone, and was thus trapped by Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie raised his own army and broke with Mangyitu. Isolated, he was finally undone by Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 要其忠義激烈，作士氣，怵寇心，皆不為徒死者。

translations.literal: In sum their fierce loyalty roused the spirit of the troops, struck fear in the rebels' hearts—they did not die in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their fierce loyalty inspired the army, struck fear into the rebels, and none of them died in vain.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，烈已！

translations.literal: Alas, how fierce their devotion!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how fierce their devotion!
